title: Strict tensor augmentation is the actual sequence adjunction unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative $A$-algebras with $A$-linear transition maps. Let $\mathscr S(B)$ be the category of strict semilinear module systems, equivalently modules over $B$ on the sequence site [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use module sheaves and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $p$ be the sequence projection with underlying inverse image the constant sequence $\Delta$, coefficient map $A\to B_n$, and canonical derived adjunction $\mathcal R=Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ of [lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction]. Let $U$ restrict each $B_n$-action to $A$, and transport this adjunction along the specified K-injective comparison $Rp_*\cong\mathcal L=R\lim U$ of [lem-coef-sequence-pushforward-limit-projections]. Write $u$ for its actual unit and $v:\mathrm{id}\to R\lim\Delta$ for the canonical derived constant-tower/limit unit [lem-coef-derived-tower-counit-projections].

For $P\in D(A)$, choose one flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $F(Q)_n=\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_n}(Q\otimes_A B_n)$, using sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with strict transitions $1\otimes b_{m,n}$. The canonical identification $F(Q)=U\mathcal R(P)$ in the derived strict tower category identifies their augmentations $\alpha_P:\Delta P\to U\mathcal R(P)$ with the single strict chain map $\alpha_Q:x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Then the following equality holds in $D(A)$, naturally in $P$:
$$u_P=R\lim(\alpha_P)\circ v_P.$$
More precisely, under the same K-flat computation, both sides equal localization of the ordinary compatible-family map $h_Q:Q\to\lim F(Q)$, $x\mapsto(x\otimes1)_n$, followed by the universal comparison $\lim F(Q)\to R\lim F(Q)$. The identifications are independent of $Q$ and are identities of the whole derived augmentation and its total limit. No flatness or surjectivity of $A\to B_n$, no boundedness of $P$, and no exactness of countable products is assumed.
